brief: A bead organizer that tucks two notch drawers into the corners where its bases meet.

requirements.evidence: 4 full bases (piece:0,0,0;full, 0,1,0, 1,0,0, 1,1,0) with 4 divided bins: 2x hex-bin-full-div2 + 2x hex-bin-full-div3; 10 small-part props (screw/nut/standoff heaps) plus tweezers staged in compartments, visible from above.

requirements.evidence: notch:0#-1,1#notch0 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) and notch:0#0,2#notch1 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) — two notch drawer frames placed.

notch:0#-1,1#notch0 stands in empty cell -1,1 beside touching bases 0,0+0,1; notch:0#0,2#notch1 stands in empty cell 0,2 beside touching bases 0,1+1,1 — both in corners where bases meet. check_build ok, meshClash clear.
requirements.requirement: tucked into the corners where its bases meet

finish.summary: Built a 2x2-base bead organizer with divided bins (2- and 3-compartment) for sorting, plus two notch drawer frames tucked into empty corner cells beside touching bases. Staged with small-part heaps and tweezers to show bead use; caps and joint bolts applied; checks clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
